papers.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
papers.problem: AI agents paste every raw tool result into their memory, which slows them down and buries the useful parts.
papers.fix: Compressing tool results cut token use by 70.01% to 89.24% and runtime by 24.45% to 55.97%, with better answers.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, agent costs and waits drop, so test compressing tool output before buying a bigger model.
papers.limitation: Tests covered web-search agents on four question-answering benchmarks and two model families only.

papers.title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.problem: Signed knowledge packs for offline AI apps prove who sent them, not that the stored vectors match the text.
papers.fix: A loose vector check lets attackers hijack answers: on a Raspberry Pi 5, correct answers fell from 0.75 to 0.39.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you ship offline search, a signature alone is not enough, so verify the vectors against the text.
papers.limitation: Results come from five text collections and two embedding models, so other setups may differ.

papers.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
papers.problem: AI programs that improve code step by step run slowly, because each round writes long text reasoning many times.
papers.fix: Small agent swarms that skip written reasoning matched rivals' 60-minute scores in a median of 3 to 8 minutes.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, small open models can search programs fast and cheaply, so try them before paying for large ones.
papers.limitation: Tests covered 21 math and science computing problems, so results on other tasks are unknown.

papers.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
papers.problem: No shared test showed whether AI agents can solve new research problems rather than recall known answers.
papers.fix: Without web access, agents solved at most 7 of 40 problems, and web success mostly came from finding published answers.
papers.practicalUseCase: Doubt claims that AI solves research problems, and check whether the agent only looked up an existing answer.
papers.limitation: The agent test used only a 50-problem math subset under one standard budget.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew what drives the size of sustainability sukuk issues, a market that is still tiny.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, equity-based contracts raised issue size, while costly second party opinions lowered it.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you follow green sukuk, expect larger deals from equity-based contracts, and watch review costs shrink issue size.
papers.limitation: The data cover 2012 to 2022, and growth is concentrated in Indonesia, Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks set up sustainability committees, but it was unclear whether Islamic banks gain as much as conventional banks.
papers.fix: In Islamic banks, committees raised only overall scores and resource reduction, while conventional banks improved on all four measures.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not assume a sustainability committee means real green products, so check what the bank actually offers.
papers.limitation: This study shows links from panel data in emerging markets, not proof of cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether AI and big data help them compete and stay sustainable.
papers.fix: AI, big data skills and data management linked to better competitiveness and sustainability, but staff digital skill helped only competitiveness.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build banking tech, invest in AI and data systems first, since staff skill alone did not lift sustainability.
papers.limitation: A survey of 214 managers at 15 Jordanian Islamic banks shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: Nobody knew how common student procrastination is, or how badly it hurts compared with other life problems.
papers.fix: Procrastination hit 72.3% of 65,950 US students and harmed grades for 45.4%, 3.5 times as often as ADHD.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you procrastinate, you have company, so treat it as the first problem to fix.
papers.limitation: Students self-reported in a survey, so it shows links, not cause, and covers only US colleges.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data showed how ADHD shapes the careers of early-career academics inside real workplaces.
papers.fix: Academia can reward people with ADHD, but social and institutional pressure often blocks that.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you have ADHD, pick workplaces that fit how you work, since the setting decides whether it helps.
papers.limitation: This interview study covers a small group of early-career academics, so it shows experiences, not rates.
